IncidentBot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Sustained 5xx spike for org=novusapi on /v1/generate (p95 latency up too). Alert threshold breached (5m). Paging oncall.
Maya (oncall): I’m up — looking. Any customer-reported impact?
Priya (Support): Novus emailed CSE — lots of client retries, some timeouts. They report production errors since ~14:02 UTC.
Jun (SRE): Logs show an increase in token churn + many long-running streams to /v1/generate. 5xx rate ~18% last 10m (baseline ~0.5%). QPS for novusapi org jumped x8.
Maya (oncall): Ok — need quick mitigation to reduce error surface. Options: temporary org-level rate override, quota slice (throttle heavy routes), or disable semantic_rerank feature toggle for this org. Thoughts?
Ethan (ENG): If semantic_rerank is causing multi-call pipelines, disabling it will drop downstream load immediately. We can flip the feature flag for org=novusapi via control plane. Low risk.
Sofia (CSE): Novus wants minimal user-visible disruption but prefers short throttling over outright feature loss. Can we do a short-lived soft-throttle?
Jun (SRE): We can apply a temporary per-org rate override +20% token allowance or alternatively cap concurrent streams to 50 for novusapi. Soft-throttle (reduce burst window) will reduce backpressure without killing requests.
Maya (oncall): Which is faster to push? I can run the admin API if you paste payload.
Ethan (ENG): Fastest is control-plane API. Jun, I can run it if you give the exact command. Sample curl:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/orgs/novusapi/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type":"rate_adjust","duration_s":600,"concurrency_limit":50,"note":"emergency soft-throttle during spike"}'
```
Jun (SRE): That will cap concurrency to 50 — good. Also recommend adding a fallback route: redirect 429s to a degraded endpoint that returns cached responses for top-10 prompts to improve UX.
Priya (Support): Novus prefers concurrency cap first. Please communicate 10m window and we’ll update customer.
Maya (oncall): I’ll authorize. Ethan — can you apply the override now and stay on call? I’ll monitor metrics.
Ethan (ENG): Applying override now.
deploy-bot: POST /admin/orgs/novusapi/overrides 200 OK (id=ovr_2b9f)
deploy-bot: override applied: concurrency_limit=50, duration_s=600, started_at=1769876550
Jun (SRE): Metrics update: 5xx down to 6% in last 2m, p95 latency trending down. QPS has stabilized but still higher than baseline.
Maya (oncall): :thumbsup: Good. Priya please ping Novus with the note: 10m soft concurrency cap applied, monitoring closely.
Priya (Support): Pinged Novus (sent at 14:16 UTC) — they acknowledged, asked for ETA to revert.
Sofia (CSE): They want a 30m follow-up. Can we extend if needed?
Maya (oncall): Yes — if traffic normalizes we will auto-expire. If not, we’ll propose staged rollback: keep cap + disable semantic_rerank after approval.
Jun (SRE): Also created a temporary traffic-shaping rule to prioritize interactive endpoints over bulk batch jobs for novusapi (rule id ts_901). That should help.
Ethan (ENG): Noted. I’ll stay on for next 10m then hand off.
deploy-bot: Monitoring alert suppressed for org=novusapi during override window.
Maya (oncall): Leaving a runbook note in the incident doc: applied concurrency cap, created ts rule, support notified. Handoff to next oncall in 12m.
Jun (SRE): Adding postmortem checklist: capture request traces for the spike, check upstream client retry behavior, and evaluate if model quantization/config led to KV cache thrash.
Priya (Support): Novus asks for visible status update once we revert — I’ll own the customer comms.
Maya (oncall): Closing loop: override expires at 1769877150 if not extended. Monitoring continues. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Ethan (ENG): :thumbsup:
Sofia (CSE): Thanks — will prep notes for post-incident customer summary.
IncidentBot: Note added to incident log (id=inc_2026_9483).
